key_highlights: ASX ended the week lower as traders braced for higher RBA rates; property market left unsupported by the central bank (#14, #63)
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical noise, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX (#65)
EV sales surpassed petrol cars in Australia for the first time, signalling a structural shift in consumer demand (#56, #44)
Housing construction expected to follow falling prices lower; Bathla collapse flags broader construction sector fragility (#64, #66)
ASX small-caps in resources (Kaoko Metals, Vanadium Resources, Piche) led weekly gains; Aurum added high-grade gold ounces (#53, #54)
Hyperscaler bond issuance competing with US Treasuries is pushing global rates higher, pressuring duration-sensitive ASX sectors (#31)
ASIC launched a review of whistleblower complaints at Big Four accounting firms, raising governance concerns (#67)
Canada's per-capita economy outperforms Australia's stalling growth, highlighting relative macro weakness (#70)

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; gold producers (Aurum) adding high-grade ounces; small-cap resources (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) outperforming
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin pressure from iron ore price softening; gold and critical-mines names offer relative strength. Monitor iron ore contract prices and Chinese demand data

sectors.trend: RBA unlikely to cut rates to support property; Victoria's sovereign debt flagged by ratings agencies; ASIC scrutiny of accounting firms raises governance risk
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from sustained higher-for-longer rates but face credit-risk headwinds from housing downturn. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) pressured by elevated borrowing costs

sectors.trend: EV sales overtook petrol cars for first time; BYD declares Australia past EV tipping point; fuel-cost avoidance driving demand but hidden infrastructure costs emerge
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WTW.AX face margin pressure from fuel-cost sensitivity; automotive and energy names (WDS.AX, WES.AX) must adapt. EV adoption accelerates structural shift in consumer spending patterns

sectors.trend: Housing construction to follow prices lower; Bathla collapse exposes 'Ponzi economy' dynamics; $3.4b industry collapse; RBA will not intervene
sectors.implications: Direct risk to construction-linked equities and REIT valuations. GPW.AX, SPG.AX, VMC.AX face occupancy and cap-rate pressure. Mortgage arrears may rise, pressuring bank NIMs

sectors.trend: Nvidia's $20B Groq deployment live this year; AI-driven security (Okta +20%); Australia faces AI worker shortage; skilled migration prioritised for AI and tradies
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX tech exposure but supports CSL.AX (healthcare tech) and BHP.AX (AI in mining). Skilled-migration policy shifts may ease labour constraints for ASX industrials

Iron ore structural shakeout vs. gold/critical-mines strength
EV adoption inflection point in Australia
Housing construction downturn and construction-sector fragility
Global bond supply (hyperscalers) pushing rates higher
Geopolitical risk premium (Iran-US, Russia-Ukraine, German far-right)
ASIC governance scrutiny of accounting sector
Australia's relative macro underperformance vs. Canada

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate path / property market stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and construction exposure; favour bank equities with strong capital buffers; monitor RBA statements and housing-credit data
Diversify away from pure iron-ore exposure (FMG.AX, BHP.AX); rotate into gold (SGR.AX, NVG.AX) and critical-mines names
Maintain 10-15% cash allocation; hold gold and energy hedges; monitor oil and LNG price spikes
Shorten duration in fixed-income portfolios; favour floating-rate and short-dated bonds; watch AUD/USD for rate-differential shifts
Avoid leveraged construction and property-development equities; monitor ASIC and Worksafe enforcement actions
Consider international diversification; monitor NOM and skilled-migration policy for labour-supply relief

opportunities.recommendation: Rotate from iron-ore majors into gold and critical-mines small-caps
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore shakeout pressures BHP/RIO/FMG; gold (Aurum) and vanadium/critical-mines names showing relative strength and ASX runner momentum

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight bank equities on sustained higher rates
opportunities.rationale: RBA unlikely to cut; NIMs supported; but monitor credit-loss provisions from housing stress

opportunities.recommendation: Position for EV-infrastructure and energy-transition beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: EV sales surpassed petrol cars; BYD confirms tipping point; charging infrastructure and grid-upgrade demand rising

defensive_moves.rationale: Housing construction following prices lower; Bathla collapse signals sector-wide fragility; RBA will not intervene

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash and gold allocation as geopolitical hedge
defensive_moves.rationale: Iran-US tensions, Russia-Ukraine conflict, and German political instability elevate tail risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Shorten bond duration; favour short-dated and floating-rate instruments
defensive_moves.rationale: Hyperscaler bond issuance competing with Treasuries is pushing global rates higher

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower over 1-3 months. Rate fears, housing-construction data, and iron ore price volatility dominate. Geopolitical headlines (Iran, Ukraine) create episodic volatility. Bull case narrative (#68) provides a floor but is offset by property and construction headwinds.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA holds and iron ore stabilises. EV transition and critical-mines demand offer structural tailwinds. However, housing downturn and construction-sector fragility cap upside. Australia's relative macro underperformance vs. Canada warrants international diversification.
